subject.title: sessions.patch has no plugin-ownership check, unlike its sessions.delete sibling

question: Should this public cross-plugin `sessions.patch` ownership bypass be handled as a narrow public gateway bugfix, or routed through security-owned advisory/backport handling first?
rationale: The source evidence supports a narrow code fix, but the affected behavior is a plugin isolation boundary on a stable gateway RPC surface, so automation should not choose disclosure and release handling on its own.

options.title: Approve narrow public fix
options.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide any release-note or backport wording.

options.title: Route through security handling
options.body: Pause public automation and handle the issue through the repository security process if maintainers consider cross-plugin session mutation advisory-worthy.

options.title: Declare patch broader by design
options.body: Keep the current behavior only if maintainers intentionally want plugin-runtime callers with admin scope to patch foreign sessions and document why delete remains different.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow public fix
recommendation.body: Patch `sessions.patch` to reuse the delete ownership invariant and add focused regression tests, while maintainers decide any release-note or backport wording.
